newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran calls for closer ties with China.
newsitem.headline: Iran calls for closer ties with China.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Sunday called for closer cooperation between his country and China, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said.

"President Rafsanjani expressed pleasure with the growing trend of Tehran-Beijing cooperation and said close cooperation between the two countries would serve to consolidate (the) peace and stability of the region," it quoted him as saying.
The Iranian leader's remarks came in a meeting with visiting Chinese Vice Premier Li Lanqing, IRNA said.
IRNA said Li "voiced Beijing's readiness to further develop economic and technical cooperation" with Iran.
China, which has angered Washington with its Iranian military ties, hopes to sell more missiles to Tehran, a Chinese industry official said in March.
Chai Zhongzhong, assistant to the president of missile builder China National Precision Machinery Import and Export Corporation, said China was only interested in selling defensive weapons to Iran.

The United States has voiced concern over Chinese sales of missiles and related technology to Iran, possibly in violation of the Missile Technology Control Regime, a 31-nation pact designed to head off missile proliferation.

U.S. officials say Iran, which has restored its capability to fire anti-ship missiles at sea, has in the past two years tripled the number of missiles deployed on its Gulf coast and is fitting Chinese-built cruise missiles to 20 of its naval boats.
